subject: microbiology
title: Opportunistic Fungal Syndromes: Mucormycosis and Pneumocystis jirovecii

steps.tx: Opportunistic invasive mycoses exploit host vulnerabilities including profound neutropenia, ketoacidosis, and T-cell immunosuppression. While angioinvasive **mucormycosis** causes acute fulminant necrosis in ketoacidosis, Pneumocystis jirovecii causes insidious subacute alveolar pneumonia in advanced acquired immunodeficiency syndrome. Distinguishing their clinical presentations, microbiological characteristics, and treatment regimens is critical on medical licensing examinations.
steps.say: Mucormycosis causes acute vascular infarction while Pneumocystis causes subacute diffuse alveolar pneumonia.

left.title: Mucormycosis syndrome
points: Onset: acute fulminant progression over days
Treatment: surgical debridement plus amphotericin B

right.title: Pneumocystis pneumonia
points: Predisposing state: CD4 count under 200 cells/uL

steps.tx: Rhino-orbital-cerebral mucormycosis begins in the nasal turbinates and paranasal sinuses, presenting with facial numbness, retro-orbital headache, proptosis, and ophthalmoplegia due to superior orbital fissure syndrome. The pathognomonic physical finding is a necrotic **black eschar** over the nasal septum, inferior turbinates, or hard palate. Direct extension through the cribriform plate or orbital apex leads to cavernous sinus thrombosis and fatal cerebral infarction.
steps.say: Invasion through facial bones produces a necrotic black palate eschar and cavernous sinus thrombosis.

vis.caption: Mucorales histology demonstrating broad, ribbon-like aseptate hyphae invading arterial lumen [Credit: CDC, StewardMD cleared]

steps.tx: A critical pharmacological risk factor for gastrointestinal and systemic mucormycosis is treatment with the iron chelator **deferoxamine**. Rhizopus species possess surface siderophore receptors that utilize ferrioxamine complexes to scavenge bound iron avidly, dramatically accelerating fungal replication. In contrast, newer second-generation iron chelators such as deferasirox and deferiprone do not promote fungal growth.
steps.say: Deferoxamine acts as a fungal siderophore, promoting explosive fungal growth by delivering iron.

nodes.label: Dialysis or thalassaemia patient receives deferoxamine chelator
Fungal receptors bind ferrioxamine complex directly
Rapid iron acquisition fuels explosive systemic fungal angioinvasion

steps.tx: The atypical unicellular fungus **Pneumocystis jirovecii**, formerly classified as a protozoan and named Pneumocystis carinii, lacks ergosterol in its cytoplasmic membrane, containing cholesterol instead. This biological distinction explains why Pneumocystis is inherently resistant to amphotericin B, fluconazole, and all other standard antifungal agents that target ergosterol synthesis or membrane integrity.
steps.say: Pneumocystis cell membranes contain cholesterol instead of ergosterol, conferring resistance to azoles and amphotericin.

rows: Cholesterol present; ergosterol is completely absent
Inherently refractory to azoles, polyenes and echinocandins

steps.tx: In patients with human immunodeficiency virus, Pneumocystis pneumonia classically presents when helper T-cell counts fall below two hundred cells per microlitre. Patients experience insidious exertional dyspnoea, dry non-productive cough, low-grade fever, and striking **exercise desaturation** where pulse oximetry saturation plummets dramatically after walking. High serum lactate dehydrogenase levels correlate with the extent of alveolar injury.
steps.say: Patients with low helper T-cell counts develop exertional hypoxaemia and elevated lactate dehydrogenase.

left.title: Clinical manifestations
points: Marked elevation of serum lactate dehydrogenase

right.title: Thoracic imaging findings
points: Spares lung apices and peripheral costophrenic angles
Upper lobe pneumatoceles prone to pneumothorax

steps.tx: Definitive diagnosis requires demonstrating fungal cysts or trophozoites in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid or induced sputum. The standard histological stain is **Gomori methenamine silver**, which highlights the thick walls of spherical, cup-shaped, or collapsed crescentic cysts measuring five to eight micrometres. A distinctive central dark dot or bracket-like thickening represents the intracystic focal wall thickening.
steps.say: Gomori silver stain outlines cup-shaped collapsed cysts with characteristic dark central brackets.

nodes.label: Obtain hypertonic saline-induced sputum or bronchoalveolar lavage
Perform Gomori methenamine silver or direct immunofluorescence
Identify 5 to 8 micrometre cup-shaped cysts with central dark dots

steps.tx: The definitive first-line therapeutic regimen is high-dose **trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole** administered intravenously or orally for twenty-one days. In patients with moderate to severe disease, defined by an arterial oxygen tension under seventy millimetres of mercury on room air or an alveolar-arterial gradient exceeding thirty-five millimetres, adjunctive systemic corticosteroids must be initiated before or concurrently with antimicrobial therapy.
steps.say: High dose trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is curative; add steroids when arterial oxygen falls below seventy.

rows: Oral prednisone 40 mg twice daily days 1-5
Taper to 40 mg daily days 6-11, then 20 mg

steps.tx: Primary chemoprophylaxis against Pneumocystis is indicated for all human immunodeficiency virus patients with CD4 counts below two hundred cells per microlitre or a history of oropharyngeal candidiasis. One double-strength **cotrimoxazole** tablet daily provides complete protection while simultaneously protecting against cerebral toxoplasmosis and Isospora enteritis. Prophylaxis may be safely discontinued once antiretroviral therapy restores CD4 counts above two hundred for three months.
steps.say: Daily cotrimoxazole protects against Pneumocystis and Toxoplasma when helper counts are under two hundred.

nodes.label: CD4 count falls below 200 cells/uL or oral thrush develops
Discontinue prophylaxis after CD4 exceeds 200 for 3 consecutive months on ART
